# glinet_reboot_schedule (Resource)

Manages the reboot schedule of the router: when it is enabled, the router reboots at `time` on the scheduled days. The router has one reboot schedule, so use one instance of this resource. When `enabled` is `false`, the provider only disables the schedule, and the router keeps its previous time and days: the configured `time` and `days` are kept in the Terraform state and get to the router only when the schedule is enabled. While the router reports the schedule as disabled, the provider does not compare `time` and `days` with the router. The write that enables the schedule (`enable`, `hour`, `min` and `week`) is taken from the web UI of the router and was not tested on a router. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The router reboots at 04:00 on Sunday and Wednesday.
resource "glinet_reboot_schedule" "this" {
  enabled = true
  time    = "04:00"
  days    = [0, 3]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `days` (Set of Number) Days of the week when the router reboots. Each day is a number from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday) (`week` in the router API).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the schedule is enabled (`enable` in the router API). When it is `true`, the router reboots at the scheduled times.
- `time` (String) Time of the reboot (`hour` and `min` in the router API). Format `HH:MM`, 24 hours, in the time zone of the router.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `reboot_schedule`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "reboot_schedule".
terraform import glinet_reboot_schedule.this reboot_schedule
```
